evidence.result: Whitespace word counts: ARI 171, PSC 154, LIB 159, CET 164; all within 150-220.
Four expected IDs, schema version, target refs, empty question_refs, required tag_ids, draft status and 2-3 source links per article verified.

limitations: The original ESA/Hubble NGC 772 URL did not load in the required source opener. Accessible NASA primary institutional sources corroborate the main NGC 772 claims but support about 100 million light-years rather than the cited ~110 million.
Native source review only; no different-provider release approval.

source_visits.note: Today's independent visits are recorded separately; the frozen source_links retain the author's 2026-10-08 access dates.

opened_sources.evidence: IAU Constellations page; lines 53-61 explain bounded sky regions and perspective; rows 107, 121, 149, 166 list Aries/Ari, Cetus/Cet, Libra/Lib, Pisces/Psc.
NASA APOD lines 242-245: Arp 78/NGC 772 in Aries, about 100 million light-years, prominent outer arm, companion NGC 770 and likely tidal interaction.
Direct open returned Internal Error. Also attempted legacy https://www.spacetelescope.org/images/potw1945a/; inaccessible.
NASA Hubble article dated 2019-11-15, lines 251-254: NGC 770 satellite distorted/disrupted NGC 772's spiral arm; NGC 772 is unbarred.
NASA M74 page lines 295-317: Pisces, 32 million light-years, symmetric spiral arms, H II regions, young stars' UV ionization.
NASA Hubble release dated 2013-03-07, lines 311-323 and 328-331: Libra, parallax, 14.5 ± 0.8 billion years and age compatibility; lines 334 includes object metadata.

Original Bond et al. 2013 paper PDF opened; lines 19-30 identify HD 140283 as a nearby subgiant, report 14.46 ± 0.31 Gyr parallax-only and about ±0.8 Gyr total error, dominated by stellar parameter/composition uncertainty; age compatible with Universe estimate.
NASA M77 page lines 295-320: Cetus, 45 million light-years, spiral/Seyfert classification, active core powered by accretion onto a supermassive black hole.

result.summary: Independent read-only review of the exact frozen ARI/PSC/LIB/CET objects. I did not author these articles. PSC, LIB, and CET are accepted; ARI needs a source-link and distance wording correction. No files were changed.

findings: IAU lists Aries/Ari. NASA APOD directly supports Arp 78 = NGC 772 in Aries, its prominent outer arm, NGC 770 as a companion, and describes tidal interactions as the likely cause. A directly opened NASA Hubble article independently states that NGC 770 distorted and disrupted the arm.

The cited ESA/Hubble URL https://esahubble.org/images/potw1945a/ returned Internal Error on direct open (the legacy spacetelescope.org URL also failed). The cited sentence attributes the arm description and ~110-million-light-year figure to that unavailable page.

Minimal correction: replace the inaccessible ESA/Hubble source with the opened NASA Hubble article https://science.nasa.gov/missions/hubble/hubble-spots-a-curious-spiral/ for NGC 770's role and the unbarred spiral classification; phrase the distance as about 100 million light-years if using the opened NASA APOD source, which gives that estimate. Preserve the original access date and state the updated access date for replacement provenance.

IAU lists Pisces/Psc; NASA's M74 page places the spiral galaxy 32 million light-years away in Pisces and supports its symmetric spiral arms, pink H II regions, hydrogen clouds, and ionization by ultraviolet light from young hot stars.
The object-specific self-check correctly explains the pink hydrogen-region glow. Schema, psc target_ref, empty question_refs, required tags, draft status, and two source links pass.

IAU lists Libra/Lib; NASA places HD 140283 in Libra and reports the 2013 Hubble age estimate 14.5 ± 0.8 billion years. The actual 2013 Bond et al. paper PDF opened and gives 14.46 ± 0.31 Gyr for parallax-only uncertainty, about ±0.8 Gyr total, with oxygen abundance an important uncertainty and compatibility with the Universe's age.

The article explicitly dates the estimate to the 2013 NASA release and does not present it as a current/latest determination. The self-check correctly treats the uncertainty as part of the measurement. Schema, lib target_ref, empty question_refs, required tags, draft status, and three links pass.

IAU lists Cetus/Cet. NASA's M77 page identifies M77 as a spiral galaxy in Cetus about 45 million light-years away and a Seyfert galaxy whose active core is powered by matter accreting onto a supermassive black hole.
The article correctly distinguishes the active nucleus from the whole galaxy and the sky region. Schema, cet target_ref, empty question_refs, required tags, draft status, and two links pass.
